decisions.reason: A rye country bread is a core everyday item built on established recipes and production, so it meets aspirations at low marginal cost and gives no trigger for search.
The premium raisin stollen is the flagship and again won a gold medal from the Deutsches Brotinstitut, which clearly exceeds aspirations, so dropping it is very unlikely.
The seeded rye mixed bread fits the established bread range and uses existing resources, so without any sign of shortfall the firm has no reason to drop it.
The dark malt rye bread is a niche variant with some risk of range pruning, but it uses the existing line and slack lets the firm carry it.
The marzipan stollen complements the award-winning stollen line in the seasonal gift assortment and is cheap to keep alongside the flagship.
The ancient grain bread is newly presented as the latest master piece and its results are still uncertain, so the firm would give it time rather than cut it early.
